clinician.trajectory_summary: A 57-year-old man presented with progressive dyspnea, fatigue, rash with petechiae, weight loss, and acute kidney injury. Physical exam revealed a grade III/VI apical systolic murmur with leaflet prolapse. Echocardiogram showed thickening of mitral valve leaflets and vegetation on the posterior leaflet, consistent with endocarditis. Blood cultures were ordered but results were not disclosed in the available case evidence. The clinical presentation and echocardiographic findings strongly support the diagnosis of Streptococcus mutans endocarditis, although direct microbiological confirmation was not available in the disclosed evidence.
